synopsis: Hazard means a potential source of harm, harm is actual injury or damage, and risk combines probability with severity; the booklet ranks a haul truck crushing a light vehicle in front of it as its number-one harm scenario [f11961, f11472]. The fatal-risk picture extends beyond people and vehicles: NIOSH's 2022 review found 85% of research cases focused on vehicle–vehicle interactions even though vehicle–environment events accounted for the largest share of reviewed fatal haul-truck accidents [f3002, f5824, f5825]. Automatic braking can introduce hazards as well as reduce them, with safe interventions depending on the machine and operation; validation must separately address failure to brake and unsafe or unnecessary braking [f1539, f808, f11966, f5816]. Regulatory duties emphasize risk reduction and evidence rather than a universal braking mandate: Australia's model WHS regulation 215 requires reasonably practicable collision-risk control and a warning device, while Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 requires risk reduction, reliable controls and technical conformity evidence [f2125, f2783, f2202]. Simulation cannot establish zero risk or cover unconceived hazards, and staged release does not establish safety beyond its operating domain; sensor models need real-measurement calibration, and highest-risk cases need physical confirmation [f995, f789, f976, f5598, f11124]. The plan should trace every requirement, test and acceptance criterion to a named hazard and explicitly state its safety boundaries; unresolved coverage includes attachment hazards outside the cited draft ISO 21815-4 scope, while software-related braking risks lack quantified collision-incident evidence [f11969, f10155, f6589, f3665].
